paper.title: A foundation machine learning potential with polarizable long-range interactions for materials modelling
paper.research_summary: We present a foundation framework that integrates explicit polarizable long-range physics with an equivariant graph neural network potential. It employs a physically motivated polarizable charge equilibration scheme that directly optimizes electrostatic interaction energies rather than partial charges. The foundation model, trained across the periodic table up to Pu, demonstrates strong performance across key materials modeling challenges. It effectively captures long-range interactions that are challenging for traditional message-passing mechanisms and accurately reproduces polarization effects under external electric fields. We have applied the model to mechanical properties, ionic diffusivity in solid-state electrolytes, ferroelectric phase transitions, and reactive dynamics at electrode-electrolyte interfaces, highlighting the model’s capacity to balance accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, we show that as a foundation model, it can be efficiently finetuned to achieve high-level accuracy for specific challenging systems.

task.task_name_raw: developing a foundation machine learning interatomic potential with polarizable long-range interactions
task.objective: to construct a mapping from atomic coordinates ri and atomic types Zi to the total potential energy Epot that integrates explicit polarizable long-range physics with an equivariant graph neural network potential
material_scope: materials across the periodic table up to Pu
periodic systems (e.g., Au2-MgO, BTA-Cu, BaTiO3, c-LLZO, β-Li3PS4/Li)
constraints: must capture long-range electrostatic and dispersion interactions explicitly
must reproduce polarization effects under external electric fields
must be transferable across diverse chemical systems and charge states
output_goal: total potential energy Epot = E0 + EPQEq + ED3
accurate prediction of materials properties and behaviors

evidence.text: To train the foundation equivariance neural network potential, we used the MPtrj dataset16 sourced from Materials Projects48 as the training dataset. All configurations were calculated using DFT with the PBE82/PBE + U83 exchange-correlation functional and pseudopotential basis.

To evaluate the capability of our framework in capturing different charge states and long-range interactions, we validated our framework against the dataset developed by Ko et al.28 and Maruf et al.38, which encompass various charge states and charge transfer systems.

evidence.text: To demonstrate the capability of our model to reproduce results from AIMD simulations, we simulate the kinetic transport properties of a solid-state electrolyte. Speciﬁcally, we investigated lithium-ion diffusivity within the cubic phase of Li7La3Zr2O12 (c-LLZO)... Figure 3a presents the Arrhenius plots derived from our model, w/o-lr model, and AIMD51 simulations.

To show the application of polarizable potentials, we performed MD simulations on a typical perovskite ferroelectric material, BaTiO3... Figure 4 illustrates the simulation results, which clearly identify four distinct phases and the three ﬁrst-order phase transitions within the simulated temperature range.

To investigate the formation of SEI, we utilized the foundation model to simulate the interfacial reactive MD of the solid electrolyte β-Li3PS4 in contact with the lithium metal anode, encompassing a system of 13,760 atoms.

stages.stage_name_raw: finetuning the foundation model for ab initio accuracy on specific challenging systems
stages.stage_goal: to adapt the foundation model to achieve quantum-accurate predictions for targeted systems through efficient finetuning
stage_input: 20% subsets of configurations from Na8/9Cl8+ clusters and Au2 dimers on MgO surfaces
mean squared force error loss function
stage_output: finetuned model with good agreement with DFT references
accurately distinguished potential energy surfaces for positive charged clusters and surface conditions

evidence.text: While our foundation model demonstrates general performance, achieving ab initio accuracy for speciﬁc systems requires ﬁnetuning. Using Na8/9Cl8+ clusters and Au2 dimers on MgO surfaces from Ko et al.28 as test cases, we performed targeted ﬁnetuning using 20% subsets of conﬁgurations and mean squared force error as the sole loss function. After ﬁnetuning, our model achieved good agreement with DFT references, accurately distinguishing potential energy surfaces for positive charged clusters and surface conditions...
